c1-gen-0061: Hagar was alone and far from home, sitting by a spring in the wild. Let's read Genesis 16:13 together.
c2-gen-0016: Sarah held her baby boy after waiting so many years. Hear her own words in Genesis 21:6 and Genesis 21:7.
c2-gen-0017: Hagar sat crying in the hot desert, and an angel called out to her. Genesis 21:17 and Genesis 21:19 carry the story on.
c2-gen-0018: Rebekah's family wanted a few more days with her at home. Listen for her answer in Genesis 24:57 and Genesis 24:58.
c2-gen-0019: The sun was going down, and travelers were coming across the land. Find Isaac in Genesis 24:63 and Genesis 24:67.
c2-gen-0020: Isaac's men dug well after well while others argued. Genesis 26:20, Genesis 26:21, and Genesis 26:22 give the names and the reason.
c3-gen-0001: A tired servant stood by the well as evening came. Hear his prayer in Genesis 24:12, Genesis 24:14, and Genesis 24:27.
c3-gen-0002: Two sons, two families, and God speaking again at Beersheba. Look at Genesis 21:12, Genesis 21:13, and Genesis 26:24 side by side.
c1-exo-0021: At the foot of the mountain, the crowd grew loud and uneasy. Let's look at Exodus 32:1.
c2-exo-0014: Gold earrings went in, and then came some hard questions. See how Aaron explains it in Exodus 32:4 and Exodus 32:24.
c2-exo-0015: Moses climbed back up the mountain, sad for his people. Stay with him in Exodus 32:31 and Exodus 32:32.
c2-exo-0016: The people were afraid to come near Moses when he came down. See his next move in Exodus 34:30 and Exodus 34:33.
c2-exo-0017: Things fell apart at the foot of the mountain that day. Exodus 32:19 and Exodus 34:1 share what God asked after that.
c2-exo-0018: Moses did not want to lead all those people on his own. Listen to the LORD in Exodus 33:14 and Exodus 33:15.
c3-exo-0001: Up on the rocky mountain, Moses asked God for something very big. Find out more in Exodus 33:18, Exodus 33:19, and Exodus 33:22.
c3-exo-0002: Moses pleaded for the people, and later God called out His own name. You can hear it in Exodus 32:13, Exodus 34:6, and Exodus 34:7.
c1-jos-0015: The long walk was over, and the people set up camp for the night. Joshua 4:19 and Joshua 4:20 name the spot.
c2-jos-0003: Someday the children would point at that pile of stones and ask. See what to say in Joshua 4:6 and Joshua 4:7.
c2-jos-0004: Achan stood before Joshua with something to admit. Joshua 7:20 and Joshua 7:21 give his own words.
c2-jos-0005: Strangers arrived with a story about coming from very far away. Check their words in Joshua 9:12 and Joshua 9:13.
c2-jos-0006: Hailstones fell, and the battle at Gibeon went on and on. Joshua 10:11, Joshua 10:12, and Joshua 10:14 describe that day.
c2-jos-0007: Everyone said yes to Joshua, but Joshua had more to say. It's all there in Joshua 24:15, Joshua 24:18, and Joshua 24:19.
c3-jos-0001: Beneath a big oak, Joshua set a large stone in place. Discover why in Joshua 4:6, Joshua 24:26, and Joshua 24:27.
c3-jos-0002: Visitors came to the camp, hoping to make a deal with Israel. Compare Joshua 4:24, Joshua 9:14, and Joshua 24:15.
c1-1sa-0010: Hannah's lips were moving, but no sound came out. See what Eli thought in First Samuel 1:13 and First Samuel 1:14.
c2-1sa-0001: Hannah finally had her baby boy, and she chose a name. First Samuel 1:20 gives her reason.
c2-1sa-0002: Hannah walked her little boy all the way to Eli. Listen to what she says in First Samuel 1:27 and First Samuel 1:28.
c2-1sa-0003: Each year Hannah made the trip to see her growing son. Find what she carried along in First Samuel 2:18 and First Samuel 2:19.
c2-1sa-0004: Hannah sang out loud to the LORD. Let's listen along in First Samuel 2:2, First Samuel 2:7, and First Samuel 2:8.
c2-1sa-0005: Young Samuel kept growing taller, year by year. Compare First Samuel 2:12 with First Samuel 2:26.
c3-1sa-0001: Samuel heard his name called in the night, and he answered. Stay close to him in First Samuel 3:10 and First Samuel 3:19.
c3-1sa-0002: For many years, a word from the LORD was rare. Walk through First Samuel 1:3, First Samuel 3:1, and First Samuel 3:21.
c1-1sa-0011: Saul was sent out on a search, with a servant by his side. First Samuel 9:3 says what was missing.
c2-1sa-0006: The elders came to Samuel with a big request. Look at First Samuel 8:5, then First Samuel 8:20.
c2-1sa-0007: Samuel was upset, so he brought it to the LORD. First Samuel 8:6 and First Samuel 8:7 hold the reply.
c2-1sa-0008: The new king was chosen, but nobody could find him! Look into First Samuel 10:21 and First Samuel 10:22.
c2-1sa-0009: Some cheered for Saul, and some grumbled. See how he handled it in First Samuel 10:24 and First Samuel 10:27.
c2-1sa-0010: Seven long days passed at Gilgal, and still no Samuel. First Samuel 13:8, First Samuel 13:9, and First Samuel 13:14 tell how it went.
c3-1sa-0003: As Samuel turned to leave, Saul grabbed hold of him. Hear Samuel's reply in First Samuel 15:27 and First Samuel 15:28.
c3-1sa-0004: Saul had an excuse each time things went wrong. Weigh his words beside Samuel's in First Samuel 13:12, First Samuel 15:21, and First Samuel 15:22.
c1-1sa-0012: The women came out dancing and singing as David came home. Their song is in First Samuel 18:6 and First Samuel 18:7.
c2-1sa-0011: Saul kept a jealous watch on David, even while David played music. Keep reading in First Samuel 18:9 and First Samuel 18:11.
c2-1sa-0012: Two friends made a secret plan with a bow and some arrows. Follow it in First Samuel 20:21 and First Samuel 20:22.
c2-1sa-0013: Deep in a dark cave, David's men whispered to him. First Samuel 24:4 and First Samuel 24:5 explain what bothered David afterward.
c2-1sa-0014: In the dark, David tiptoed through a sleeping camp. Go with him through First Samuel 26:11, First Samuel 26:12, and First Samuel 26:16.
c2-1sa-0015: Brave men from Jabesh Gilead walked all night to bring Saul home. First Samuel 31:11 and First Samuel 31:13 finish the story.
c3-1sa-0005: Two best friends had to say goodbye. Read their parting words in First Samuel 18:3 and First Samuel 20:42.
c3-1sa-0006: David stood outside the cave and called out to King Saul. Listen in First Samuel 24:12, First Samuel 24:15, and First Samuel 26:10.
c1-ezr-0001: A mighty king in Persia sent a message across his whole land. Ezra 1:1 and Ezra 1:2 hold his words.
c2-ezr-0001: The people were back in Jerusalem, but they felt scared of their neighbors. See what they did in Ezra 3:3 and Ezra 3:6.
c2-ezr-0002: Trumpets sounded, and the singers took turns as the builders finished the base. Let's hear Ezra 3:11.
c2-ezr-0003: Ezra made the long trip home to Jerusalem. Ezra 7:6 describes the man himself.
c2-ezr-0004: Some people shouted, and some cried out loud, all at the same time. Ezra 3:12 and Ezra 3:13 let us hear it.
c2-ezr-0005: At last the work was done, and the people gathered. Find how they marked it in Ezra 6:15, Ezra 6:16, and Ezra 6:22.
c3-ezr-0001: The hand of God was on Ezra for his whole trip. Ezra 7:6, Ezra 7:9, and Ezra 7:10 explain why.
c3-ezr-0002: Kings far away were moved to help God's people go home. Start with Ezra 1:1, then Ezra 6:22.
c1-neh-0001: Nehemiah ended his prayer with one more request. Look at the very end of Nehemiah 1:11.
c2-neh-0001: Bad news came about Jerusalem's broken walls and gates. Nehemiah 1:3 and Nehemiah 1:4 say how Nehemiah took it.
c2-neh-0002: The people stood listening to God's Law, and many were in tears. Hear Nehemiah's words in Nehemiah 8:9 and Nehemiah 8:10.
c2-neh-0003: Enemies made fun of the wall, even joking about a fox. Nehemiah 4:3 and Nehemiah 4:6 let us see the wall rise.
c2-neh-0004: At night, Nehemiah went out alone to see the broken walls. Follow his secret trip in Nehemiah 2:12, Nehemiah 2:15, and Nehemiah 2:18.
c2-neh-0005: From early morning until noon, the crowd listened to the Law. Picture that crowd in Nehemiah 8:3 and Nehemiah 8:5.
c3-neh-0001: Nehemiah faced a big question from the king, and later, enemies close by. Compare Nehemiah 2:4 with Nehemiah 4:9.
c3-neh-0002: Fifty-two days on the wall, with enemies watching all around. Nehemiah 4:20, Nehemiah 6:15, and Nehemiah 6:16 bring it to an end.
c1-ezr-0002: Ezra sat still and shocked until evening came. Ezra 9:3 and Ezra 9:5 say what he did when he got up.
c2-ezr-0006: Ezra began a very honest prayer to God. Start right at Ezra 9:6.
c2-neh-0006: Nehemiah came back and found a surprise inside God's house. Nehemiah 13:7 and Nehemiah 13:8 tell what he did about it.
c2-neh-0007: Sellers kept coming on the Sabbath, and evening was falling. Walk with Nehemiah through Nehemiah 13:19.
c2-ezr-0007: Ezra remembered years of hard times far from home. Look at Ezra 9:8 and Ezra 9:9 together.
c2-neh-0008: The prayer remembers the people turning away, again and again. Then comes a big turn in Nehemiah 9:16 and Nehemiah 9:17.
c3-neh-0003: The people poured out all their troubles to God. See what they said about Him in Nehemiah 9:32 and Nehemiah 9:33.
c3-ezr-0003: Ezra closed his prayer with no excuses at all. Think along with him in Ezra 9:13 and Ezra 9:15.
c1-psa-0018: A traveler wonders out loud where help will come from. Hear the reply in Psalm 121:1 and Psalm 121:2.
c2-psa-0008: The writer thinks about how God made him, inside and out. Psalm 139:14 is a song worth saying out loud.
c2-psa-0009: This psalm is a sorry prayer, asking God to wash away wrong. Psalm 51:10 holds one of its biggest requests.
c2-psa-0010: Hyssop was a little plant used for washing. Say Psalm 51:7 out loud and keep listening.
c2-psa-0011: God says He will guide us along the way. Psalm 32:8 and Psalm 32:9 give a warning, too.
c2-psa-0012: Like a mother bird with her wings spread wide, this psalm is full of pictures. Look at Psalm 91:2 and Psalm 91:4.
c3-psa-0002: Up in the sky or across the farthest sea, where could anyone go? Psalm 139:7, Psalm 139:9, and Psalm 139:10 wonder about it.
c3-psa-0003: One man decided to stop hiding his wrong things from God. Put Psalm 32:5, Psalm 51:16, and Psalm 51:17 side by side.
c1-psa-0019: This psalm retells God's great works, from the stars to the wilderness. Listen for the pattern in Psalm 136:1 and Psalm 136:26.
c2-psa-0013: Psalm 78 is a long song about God's works in the past. Begin with Psalm 78:4 and Psalm 78:6.
c2-psa-0014: A small family wandered from land to land, and kings took notice. Hear God's words in Psalm 105:14 and Psalm 105:15.
c2-psa-0015: After the trouble at Horeb, the people were in real danger. Psalm 106:23 is about Moses in that moment.
c2-psa-0016: The people came back to God, but something was wrong. Psalm 78:35, Psalm 78:36, and Psalm 78:37 explain it.
c2-psa-0017: God remembered what He said to Israel's fathers long ago. You'll find it in Psalm 105:8 and Psalm 105:11.
c3-psa-0004: From watching sheep to leading a nation, Psalm 78:70, Psalm 78:71, and Psalm 78:72 follow David.
c3-psa-0005: Two psalms look back at God and His people in hard times. Compare Psalm 78:38 with Psalm 106:44 and Psalm 106:45.
c1-pro-0018: Wisdom is pictured as a woman calling out for all to hear. Proverbs 1:20 and Proverbs 1:21 say where.
c2-pro-0008: Wisdom's warning comes to a close. Hear her last words in Proverbs 1:32 and Proverbs 1:33.
c2-pro-0009: Wisdom calls out to everyone who will listen. Proverbs 8:11 is part of her speech.
c2-pro-0010: Charm can fool people, and pretty looks don't last. Proverbs 31:30 finishes the thought.
c2-pro-0011: Wisdom speaks to two different groups of people. Hear both in Proverbs 1:28 and Proverbs 8:17.
c2-pro-0012: Correcting someone isn't always easy. Proverbs 9:7 and Proverbs 9:8 give wise advice about it.
c3-pro-0002: Before the mountains were in place, Wisdom was right there. Look at Proverbs 8:27 and Proverbs 8:30.
c3-pro-0003: Two voices call from two different houses, saying almost the same thing. Weigh Proverbs 9:16, Proverbs 9:18, and Proverbs 8:35.
c1-dan-0017: Belshazzar's feast was loud and crowded, until everything stopped. Daniel 5:5 says why.
c2-dan-0001: The king asked his advisors for something impossible. Hear their nervous reply in Daniel 2:10 and Daniel 2:11.
c2-dan-0002: Daniel hurried home and told his three friends the scary news. Daniel 2:17 and Daniel 2:18 follow the four of them.
c2-dan-0003: A mystery stone flew at the giant statue in the king's dream. Daniel 2:34 and Daniel 2:35 finish the picture.
c2-dan-0004: A messenger from heaven called out about a tall tree. Daniel 4:14 and Daniel 4:17 explain the reason.
c2-dan-0005: Daniel stood before the king and read the strange words. Listen to Daniel 5:25 and Daniel 5:27.
c3-dan-0001: God showed Daniel the king's secret in the night. Hear Daniel's thank-you prayer in Daniel 2:20 and Daniel 2:23.
c3-dan-0002: Daniel reminded King Belshazzar of an old story about Nebuchadnezzar. Connect Daniel 4:34, Daniel 4:37, and Daniel 5:22.
c1-jer-0001: God's word came to a young man named Jeremiah. Jeremiah 1:4 and Jeremiah 1:5 hold what God said.
c2-jer-0001: Down at the potter's house, the wheel was spinning. Watch closely in Jeremiah 18:3 and Jeremiah 18:4.
c2-jer-0002: Jeremiah had lots of words from God to get down on a scroll. Jeremiah 36:2 and Jeremiah 36:4 name the writer.
c2-jer-0003: Jeremiah sank down in the mud at the bottom of a deep pit. Find out who spoke up in Jeremiah 38:7 and Jeremiah 38:9.
c2-jer-0004: Jeremiah felt too young to speak for God. See what happened next in Jeremiah 1:6 and Jeremiah 1:9.
c2-jer-0005: Jeremiah wrote a letter to the people living far away. Jeremiah 29:10 and Jeremiah 29:11 come from that letter.
c3-jer-0001: The people were far from home, wondering if God was still near. Jeremiah 29:12, Jeremiah 29:13, and Jeremiah 29:14 speak to them.
c3-jer-0002: A king cut up the scroll, piece by piece. Jeremiah 36:23, Jeremiah 36:32, and Jeremiah 31:33 come after that.
c1-jer-0002: Jeremiah stood at the gate and spoke to everyone coming in. Jeremiah 7:2 and Jeremiah 7:4 hold his warning.
c2-jer-0006: People did wrong all week, then came to worship as if nothing happened. Hear God's question in Jeremiah 7:10 and Jeremiah 7:11.
c2-jer-0007: Jeremiah walked to the Potsherd Gate with some elders and a flask. Jeremiah 19:10 and Jeremiah 19:11 say what to do.
c2-jer-0008: People laughed at Jeremiah every day, and he wanted to stop speaking. His honest words are in Jeremiah 20:8 and Jeremiah 20:9.
c2-jer-0009: Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke off Jeremiah's neck in front of everyone. Jeremiah 28:10 and Jeremiah 28:13 give God's reply.
c2-jer-0010: Jeremiah warned the people not to be fooled by tricky voices. Read his letter in Jeremiah 29:7 and Jeremiah 29:8.
c3-jer-0003: God asks a big question about how near and far He is. Think about Jeremiah 23:23 and Jeremiah 23:24.
c3-jer-0004: Some voices kept saying everything would be fine. Hear both sides in Jeremiah 23:17, Jeremiah 28:2, and Jeremiah 28:9.
c1-ezk-0001: Ezekiel was a priest living far from home among the captives. Ezekiel 1:1 and Ezekiel 1:3 say where he was.
c2-ezk-0001: Ezekiel's first vision reached its end. Ezekiel 1:28 says what he did.
c2-ezk-0002: God had a strong message for the leaders called shepherds. Let's look at Ezekiel 34:2 and Ezekiel 34:3.
c2-ezk-0003: A whole valley full of bones lay out under the sky. Ezekiel 37:2 and Ezekiel 37:3 hold Ezekiel's reply to God's question.
c2-ezk-0004: Rattle, rattle, the bones came together, bone to bone. See the ending in Ezekiel 37:7 and Ezekiel 37:10.
c2-ezk-0005: The sheep were scattered, and their shepherds were no help. The LORD speaks up in Ezekiel 34:10 and Ezekiel 34:11.
c3-ezk-0001: God spoke to His scattered people far from home. Take in Ezekiel 36:25 and Ezekiel 36:26.
c3-ezk-0002: Twice, God talks about putting His Spirit inside His people. Hold Ezekiel 36:27 next to Ezekiel 37:14.
c1-ezk-0002: God called Ezekiel 'Son of man' and began to give him a job. Ezekiel 2:1 and Ezekiel 2:2 come first.
c2-ezk-0006: God sent Ezekiel to people who might not listen at all. Ezekiel 2:5 and Ezekiel 2:7 explain what they would learn.
c2-ezk-0007: Someone held out a scroll covered in sad words on both sides. God speaks to Ezekiel in Ezekiel 3:1 and Ezekiel 3:2.
c2-ezk-0008: People kept repeating an old saying about sour grapes. God answers it in Ezekiel 18:2 and Ezekiel 18:4.
c2-ezk-0009: A watchman spots danger and blows the trumpet loud. Picture the scene through Ezekiel 33:3 and Ezekiel 33:5.
c2-ezk-0010: God warned Ezekiel that the people would not listen to him. So God got him ready, in Ezekiel 3:7 and Ezekiel 3:9.
c3-ezk-0003: The people grumbled about God's ways. Hear how He answers in Ezekiel 18:25 and Ezekiel 18:29.
c3-ezk-0004: Ezekiel was a watchman, calling people to turn around. Ezekiel 33:7, Ezekiel 33:9, and Ezekiel 18:32 explain God's reason.
c1-luk-0036: Zacharias the priest was on duty when the lot fell to him. Luke 1:8 and Luke 1:9 say what he was chosen to do.
c2-luk-0005: Everyone was guessing the baby's name, and Zacharias couldn't say a word. Luke 1:62 and Luke 1:63 tell what he did.
c2-luk-0006: Mary sang a song about big surprises from God. Sing along in Luke 1:52 and Luke 1:53.
c2-mat-0012: Matthew begins with a long family list. The very first verse, Matthew 1:1, sets it up.
c2-luk-0007: Old Simeon had waited many years in Jerusalem. Luke 2:26 and Luke 2:30 hold his words.
c2-luk-0008: Anna walked in at just the right moment. Take a look at Luke 2:37 and Luke 2:38.
c3-mat-0001: Matthew counts the generations in three groups of fourteen. Count along in Matthew 1:11, Matthew 1:12, and Matthew 1:17.
c3-luk-0001: Two angel visits, two very different moments. Compare Luke 1:18, Luke 1:20, and Luke 1:45.
c1-mat-0035: Jesus and His friends traveled to a new area, and He asked them a question. Matthew 16:13 names the place.
c2-mat-0013: Crowds had gone out to the wild country to see John. Jesus speaks about him in Matthew 11:9 and Matthew 11:10.
c2-mat-0014: Jesus turned to His closest friends with a question just for them. Hear Peter speak up in Matthew 16:15 and Matthew 16:16.
c2-mat-0015: High on the mountain, Peter was so excited he spoke right up. Matthew 17:4 has his idea.
c2-mat-0016: Jesus was changed right in front of His disciples on the mountain. Matthew 17:2 and Matthew 17:3 say who was there.
c2-mat-0017: A voice spoke from the cloud, and the disciples bowed low. Come close to Matthew 17:6 and Matthew 17:7.
c3-mat-0002: The disciples heard a voice from the cloud above. Stay on that mountain with Matthew 17:5 and Matthew 17:8.
c3-mat-0003: John sat in prison and sent his friends with a question. Matthew 11:3, Matthew 11:4, and Matthew 16:17 belong together here.
c1-mrk-0022: Jesus spoke plainly about hard days ahead. Mark 8:31 and Mark 8:32 say how Peter reacted.
c2-mrk-0002: A man brought his son to Jesus, hoping for a miracle. Hear the cry in Mark 9:23 and Mark 9:24.
c2-mrk-0003: Jesus placed a little child right in the middle of His friends. Mark 9:36 and Mark 9:37 picture the moment.
c2-mrk-0004: A man said he had kept every rule since he was young. Mark 10:20 and Mark 10:21 let us watch Jesus look at him.
c2-mrk-0005: The man walked away sad, holding on to all he owned. Mark 10:22 and Mark 10:25 give Jesus' words after.
c2-mrk-0006: A teacher of the Law agreed with Jesus. Mark 12:33 and Mark 12:34 give Jesus' answer to him.
c3-mrk-0001: One widow came with two tiny coins. Mark 12:42, Mark 12:43, and Mark 12:44 share what Jesus said.
c3-mrk-0002: On the road, the disciples argued about who was the greatest. Mark 9:35, Mark 10:37, and Mark 10:43 bring Jesus' reply.
c1-jhn-0032: Supper was going on when Jesus stood up from the table. Follow Him in John 13:4 and John 13:5.
c2-jhn-0011: Jesus came to Peter with a bowl of water, and Peter was surprised. Hear him in John 13:6 and John 13:8.
c2-jhn-0012: Jesus told His friends not to be troubled. Let's read John 14:1 and John 14:2 together.
c2-jhn-0013: One of the disciples was puzzled and said so out loud. John 14:4 and John 14:5 name him.
c2-jhn-0014: Jesus talked about a vine and its branches. Look at John 15:4 and John 15:5.
c2-jhn-0015: Around the supper table, Jesus talked with His followers about who they were. John 15:14 and John 15:15 give His words.
c3-jhn-0001: Jesus prayed for His followers before His hardest night. Notice what repeats in John 17:11, John 17:21, and John 17:22.
c3-jhn-0002: These verses come from Jesus' last night with His friends: John 13:1, John 15:12, and John 17:26.
c1-act-0031: The church was growing fast, and a complaint came up. Acts 6:1 explains it.
c2-act-0010: The twelve needed seven trusted helpers. Acts 6:3 and Acts 6:4 lay out the plan.
c2-act-0011: False witnesses spoke against Stephen in front of the council. Acts 6:13 and Acts 6:15 describe that room.
c2-act-0012: Angry men were all around, and Stephen gazed up. Hear his words in Acts 7:55 and Acts 7:56.
c2-act-0013: Cornelius gave to people in need and prayed often. An angel visits him in Acts 10:2 and Acts 10:4.
c2-act-0014: Some people were upset that Peter ate with Gentiles. The talk ends in Acts 11:3 and Acts 11:18.
c3-act-0001: Leaders in Jerusalem wrote a careful letter to new believers. Acts 15:24 and Acts 15:28 come from it.
c3-act-0002: Peter saw a vision in Joppa and visited a home in Caesarea. Line up Acts 10:15, Acts 10:28, and Acts 15:9.
c1-rom-0017: Romans 8 begins with big words for people in Christ Jesus. Let's read Romans 8:1 together.
c2-rom-0002: Paul writes about the Spirit of adoption. Romans 8:15 gives the words we cry out.
c2-rom-0003: Sometimes we don't know what to pray. Romans 8:26 is for moments like that.
c2-rom-0004: Paul asks a big question, then another. Finish the thought in Romans 8:31.
c2-rom-0005: The Spirit speaks to our spirit, Paul says. Romans 8:16 and Romans 8:17 keep going from there.
c2-rom-0006: Paul asks believers to give their whole selves to God. Romans 12:1 and Romans 12:2 say why.
c3-rom-0001: Paul thinks about hard times right now. Keep reading through Romans 8:17 and Romans 8:18.
c3-rom-0002: Trouble, hunger, danger, and the sword are all on Paul's list. Romans 8:28, Romans 8:35, and Romans 8:37 walk through them.
c1-1co-0008: In Corinth, people kept naming their favorite leaders. Paul answers in First Corinthians 1:12 and First Corinthians 1:13.
c2-1co-0002: To some, the message of the cross sounds silly. First Corinthians 1:18 says what it is to us.
c2-1co-0003: Paul wrote plainly to the church in Corinth. Read along with First Corinthians 3:1 and First Corinthians 3:2.
c2-1co-0004: Few words or many words? Paul weighs them in First Corinthians 14:19.
c2-1co-0005: Paul reminds the believers in Corinth who they are. Let's sit with First Corinthians 3:16 and First Corinthians 3:17.
c2-1co-0006: Paul thought about how his choices might hurt a brother. First Corinthians 8:1 and First Corinthians 8:13 hold his decision.
c3-1co-0001: Some went hungry at the church supper while others had plenty. First Corinthians 11:21 and First Corinthians 11:33 give Paul's advice.
c3-1co-0002: Paul wanted the church in Corinth to get along. First Corinthians 1:10, First Corinthians 14:33, and First Corinthians 14:40 connect his thoughts.
c1-gal-0009: After meeting Jesus, Paul didn't rush to see the apostles. Galatians 1:16 and Galatians 1:17 say where he went.
c2-gal-0002: Paul says the message he shared did not come from people. Galatians 1:11 and Galatians 1:12 explain more.
c2-gal-0003: The leaders shook hands with Paul and Barnabas. Galatians 2:9 and Galatians 2:10 add one more request.
c2-gal-0004: Before faith came, the law kept watch like a guard. Galatians 3:23 and Galatians 3:24 keep the picture going.
c2-gal-0005: Paul names many kinds of people: Jew and Greek, slave and free. Hear the end of it in Galatians 3:26 and Galatians 3:28.
c2-gal-0006: At just the right time in history, God acted. Galatians 4:4 and Galatians 4:7 follow what that means for you.
c3-gal-0001: Paul tells the Galatians to stand firm and stay free. Galatians 5:1 and Galatians 5:6 point to what really counts.
c3-gal-0002: Paul looks way back, hundreds of years before the law. Galatians 3:6, Galatians 3:17, and Galatians 3:18 trace the story.
c1-2co-0001: Paul says we carry a treasure. Second Corinthians 4:7 says where he keeps it.
c2-2co-0001: Paul pairs each hard day with a 'yet.' Follow along in Second Corinthians 4:8 and Second Corinthians 4:9.
c2-2co-0002: Our bodies get older, Paul says, but he doesn't give up. Second Corinthians 4:16 says more.
c2-2co-0003: What happens when someone is in Christ? Let's read Second Corinthians 5:17 together.
c2-2co-0004: Paul says God gave us a special job to do. Second Corinthians 5:18 and Second Corinthians 5:20 name the people who do it.
c2-2co-0005: Paul compares giving to planting seeds in a field. Second Corinthians 9:6 and Second Corinthians 9:7 grow the idea.
c3-2co-0001: Paul talks about what we can see and what we can't. Second Corinthians 4:17 and Second Corinthians 4:18 explore both.
c3-2co-0002: Paul brags about his struggles, which seems strange at first. Second Corinthians 4:7, Second Corinthians 12:9, and Second Corinthians 12:10 connect it all.
c1-2ti-0001: Paul remembers Timothy's grandmother and mother. Second Timothy 1:5 names them both.
c2-2ti-0001: Paul sends young Timothy a reminder. Second Timothy 1:5 and Second Timothy 1:6 hold it.
c2-2ti-0002: Paul reminds Timothy what kind of spirit God gives. Second Timothy 1:7 names it.
c2-2ti-0003: Paul encourages Timothy to do his very best for God. Hear Paul's words in Second Timothy 2:15.
c2-2ti-0004: Timothy learned the Scriptures when he was just a little boy. Paul reminds him in Second Timothy 3:14 and Second Timothy 3:15.
c2-2ti-0005: All Scripture is useful, Paul says, in many ways. Second Timothy 3:16 and Second Timothy 3:17 list them.
c3-2ti-0001: Near the end of his life, Paul thinks about a crown. Second Timothy 4:6 and Second Timothy 4:8 say who else gets one.
c3-2ti-0002: Paul looks back like a runner at the finish line. Second Timothy 1:5, Second Timothy 3:15, and Second Timothy 4:7 tie it together.
c1-1pe-0001: Peter starts his letter full of praise. Let's read First Peter 1:3.
c2-1pe-0001: Peter describes something that never spoils or fades. First Peter 1:4 points to where it waits.
c2-1pe-0002: They had never met Jesus in person, yet they believed. First Peter 1:8 describes how they felt.
c2-1pe-0003: Someone asks you why you trust Jesus. First Peter 3:15 says how to answer.
c2-1pe-0004: Peter uses big, royal words for believers. First Peter 2:9 and First Peter 2:10 look back at before.
c2-1pe-0005: Peter says to hand all your worries over to God. First Peter 5:6 and First Peter 5:7 give the reason.
c3-1pe-0001: A roaring lion is a scary picture. First Peter 5:8 and First Peter 5:9 say what to do.
c3-1pe-0002: Peter writes to believers going through hard trials. Hold First Peter 1:6, First Peter 1:7, and First Peter 5:9 together.
c1-1jn-0001: John passes along a message he heard straight from Jesus. It's in First John 1:5.
c2-1jn-0001: What happens when we tell God what we did wrong? Find out in First John 1:9.
c2-1jn-0002: Nobody knows yet all that we will become, John says. First John 3:2 looks ahead.
c2-1jn-0003: John writes a short verse with a big reason in it. It's waiting in First John 4:19.
c2-1jn-0004: Twice in one chapter, John says the same thing about God. Compare First John 4:8 with First John 4:16.
c2-1jn-0005: John explains why he wrote his letter. Look for it in First John 5:11 and First John 5:13.
c3-1jn-0001: John compares two different ways to walk. First John 1:6 and First John 1:7 lay them out.
c3-1jn-0002: John looks at God sending His Son for us. Follow First John 4:7, First John 4:10, and First John 4:18 to the end.
